tier_reason: README tables compare kmeans_rgb/kmeans against skmeans with the harness public in js_bench/src/vector.ts, rgb.ts and images.ts (same 100-iteration cap, threshold 0 so kmeans-wasm never exits early, skmeans' own kmrand seeding, inputs built outside the timer); build flags are public in Cargo.toml (release: opt-level 3, LTO, codegen-units 1, panic abort; wasm-opt -O4) and .cargo/config.toml (+simd128), and the CPU (AMD Ryzen 5 9600X) and runtime (Node.js 26.10.0) are stated. Only the exact rustc version is unpinned (rust-version 1.98 minimum).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust (edition 2024, rust-version 1.98 minimum; exact rustc version not stated) built with wasm-pack build --release --target nodejs; Cargo.toml [profile.release] opt-level = 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1, panic = abort, strip; .cargo/config.toml rustflags -C target-feature=+simd128 for wasm32-unknown-unknown; wasm-opt -O4 --enable-simd --enable-bulk-memory --enable-nontrapping-float-to-int. Harness: js_bench/src/vector.ts, rgb.ts, images.ts (TypeScript, Node).
corrections.caveats: First-party; most of the code and the harness since v3.2.0 were written by AI assistants (README says so). The baseline skmeans is a naive Lloyd k-means in plain JavaScript that scans all n*k distances every round, while kmeans-wasm uses Hamerly bounds and, for the packed RGB/RGBA entry points, collapses the input to its distinct colours with weights; most of the speed-up is algorithmic, not from wasm or SIMD, and the README says the image speed-up falls from 84x to 13x as the distinct-colour share grows. No stronger JS k-means (e.g. a bounds-based one) is compared. Small or k=2 cases are level or slower (1,000 pixels, 2 colours 0.9x; 100,000 pixels, 2 colours 1.1x). Real-image skmeans timings are one measured run after one warm-up. Seeds differ per run on both sides (random distinct input points vs skmeans kmrand), so the two sides can converge to different local minima; kmeans-wasm always runs all 100 iterations (threshold 0) while skmeans may stop early, which favours skmeans. 2 stars.

notes: README numbers match the record exactly (10,000 x 50 x 10: 83.15 vs 1456.35 ms, 17.5x; 100,000 RGB px, 32 colours 247.03 vs 1677.87 ms, 6.8x; blue-marble 16 colours 109.24 vs 11133.62 ms, 101.8x; 1,000 px 2 colours 0.47 vs 0.41 ms, 0.9x). Flags are public in the repo's build config, so A stands; record the shortcoming that the win is mostly algorithmic (Hamerly bounds plus distinct-colour dedup) against a naive JS baseline, with single-sample skmeans image runs and a tiny project (2 stars, AI-written). License MIT (LICENSE_MIT), last commit 2026-09-27 (release v3.7.0), not a fork.

corrections.claimed_speedup: renderToHtml (medium fixture): md4x.wasm 15.08 us/iter vs markdown-it 72.68 us/iter, ~4.8x (derived from page data); md4x.napi (native) 7.38 us/iter, 9.85x faster than markdown-it and 2.05x faster than md4x.wasm per the page summary; md4w 17.40 us in the same table. parseAST (medium): md4x.wasm 28.12 us vs markdown-it 50.44 us, ~1.8x (derived from page data), and here md4w (23.07 us) and ox-content (17.54 us) beat md4x.wasm. README headline '~8x faster than markdown-it' refers to the native NAPI build, not wasm.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig (build.zig.zon minimum_zig_version 0.16.0; exact version not stated); zig build wasm builds md4x.wasm for wasm32-wasi with +simd128, link_libc, single_threaded, optimize = ReleaseFast (pkg_optimize), stripped; NAPI via zig build napi-all at ReleaseFast. Bench source packages/md4x/bench/index.mjs (mitata).
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark run under Bun (JavaScriptCore), not V8 or a browser, on one medium fixture only (small and large are commented out in index.mjs). markdown-it runs with its default preset while md4x enables GFM and its own extensions, so outputs are not byte-equivalent; the README notes the parsers return different AST shapes and that the parseAST leaders are within run-to-run noise. In parseAST, md4x.wasm is slower than md4w and ox-content. The '~8x' headline is the native NAPI addon. md4x is a Zig port of mity/md4c (catalogued in wave 3, compared against cmark) and was earlier a C wrapper of it (md4x-c); md4w (ije/md4w, another md4c wasm build) is listed separately.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly; claimed_speedup extended with the parseAST group, where md4x.wasm wins only ~1.8x over markdown-it and loses to md4w. Flags are in build.zig, so the other search record for the same repo (paper:md4x-aslang-registry, tier C, category assemblyscript-and-wasm-langs) understated the evidence; fold one into the other. md4x is a Zig port of the already-listed mity/md4c (wave 3); by the ports-are-duplicates precedent the orchestrator may record it as duplicate, though its claim (wasm/NAPI vs markdown-it in JS) differs from md4c's native vs cmark claim. MIT, last commit 2026-09-13, not a fork.
